title: City-funded nonprofits that lobby Sacramento
question: Which nonprofits the City pays also pay lobbyists at the State Capitol, on what, and do their tax returns say so?
finding: 13 nonprofits among the City's largest payees filed lobbyist-employer reports with the Secretary of State since 2015, showing $4.3 million paid for lobbying. 7 of them answer no to the lobbying question on tax returns covering periods in which their own State reports show lobbying payments: The Exploratorium ($184,000); Project Open Hand ($139,500); PRC ($114,189); National Harm Reduction Coalition ($73,500); Glide Foundation ($72,250); Mission Neighborhood Centers Inc ($34,500). Much of the lobbying is for State budget money: several reports name a budget request for the organization's own project.
how: Organizations that pay for lobbying file lobbyist-employer reports (Form 635) with the Secretary of State, one for each calendar quarter. Every such report filed under the name of one of the 233 largest City payees was read, the latest version of each quarter kept, and its four summary payment lines (A to D) added. The firm names come from the employer's registrations (Form 602). The subject is the most recent report that names bills or agencies, cut to 25 words. Tax returns: for each Form 990 on file, the yes/no lobbying question and the lobbying-fees line were set against the State reports whose quarter ends inside that tax year. State awards are from the California Grants Portal for State fiscal years 2022-23 to 2024-25.
limits: City money is not shown to have paid for any of it. A nonprofit can truthfully answer no on its tax return if the lobbying was done by a separate affiliate or a sponsored project that files its own return, or if the State reports cover work, such as the contacts with State agencies they list, that it did not treat as lobbying for tax purposes; that is a question for the organization. Only the 233 largest payees were searched and only exact names matched, so the list is short and incomplete. Dropped as a different organization of the same name: Meals On Wheels (the State filer gives San Diego; the City payee's tax return gives San Francisco). The Tides Center files separate reports for several projects it sponsors; they are added together here.
